leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer B043 as a single-part prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, framed around the physiology of GLP-1 and identification of its active form. They share the view that the discovery chain is complete without the drug-development step. They do not share a settled view of Mojsov's priority relative to the Habener group: Sandberg names a Drucker-Holst-Knudsen trio as the fallback if the record proves insufficient, Wahren-Herlenius holds her preference loosely, and the chair would reopen the third seat if colleagues think the physiology-only versus physiology-plus-development framing should decide it.

Three members prefer B043 as a single-part prize to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, with a citation that links the physiology of GLP-1 to long-acting therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity. They share the view that the translational step is decisive and that Mojsov's contested priority is a risky basis for the third seat. They differ in confidence: Perlmann moved to this trio from a Mojsov trio in his opening and says it is not settled, and Linnarsson says he is not certain it is better. Both trios agree on Drucker and Holst; the disagreement is confined to one seat.

areas_of_agreement: All six members explicitly prefer B043 (GLP-1 and incretin therapies) as the first and only prize part, and all six statements describe the scientific arc, the independent confirmation of the mechanism, the randomized outcome evidence and the maturity of recognition as strong.
All six prefer a one-part prize, citing that a three-laureate limit divided across two parts would force thinner attribution on B043 or on a second candidate.
Drucker and Holst are named by all six members; only the third seat (Mojsov or Knudsen) differs.

Every member states that the Mojsov priority question relative to the Habener group, who are not among the credited names, cannot be settled from the supplied material and needs the primary publication record.
Members on both sides say an industrial setting should not by itself exclude Knudsen, and that the choice should rest on independent scientific contribution.
scientific_disputes: Whether the citation should cover physiology only (the active peptide, its actions and receptor biology) or physiology plus the development of long-acting agonists, which in effect decides whether the third seat reflects discovery or translation.
Whether B005 (optogenetics) is a serious competitor given that it is a method award; members rank it from second to fifth, and four members list it as an alternative.

Whether B010 (unfolded protein response) is strong enough on fundamental physiology when clinical translation, including ISRIB-type modulators, is still prospective; five members list it as an alternative, and Perlmann and Sandberg question how much weight a basic-mechanism prize should carry.
Whether B049 (cGAS-STING) is premature because no STING-targeted therapy has been validated; Sandberg treats it as a future candidate and Wahren-Herlenius would put it behind B010 this year.
attribution_disputes: B043: Mojsov versus Knudsen for the third seat. Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is called a discovery-level step by her supporters, but her priority relative to the Habener group is unresolved. Knudsen's role in liraglutide and semaglutide is not disputed, but her place is argued against on the grounds of industrial drug development.
B043: Habener is not in the credited list, so members on both sides say any trio looks incomplete.

B005: six credited names (Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenboeck, Nagel) against three seats; members disagree on whether the unit is channel discovery or neuronal application, and every trio leaves out someone with a serious claim.
B010: members note that the omission of Ron and Kaufman may weaken the Walter and Mori pair, although Sandberg and El-Manira regard it as the cleanest attribution on the shortlist.
B008: Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius say Eshhar and other early CAR originators outside the credited names leave the CAR-T credit incomplete.
maturity_disputes: B043 is judged mature by all six members; the open maturity points are long-term safety and durability of chronic incretin therapy, noted by Linnarsson.
B010 is called long overdue by some members, while Perlmann cautions that age alone does not make it overdue and that its medical case is still developing.
B049 is argued to be early because STING-directed therapy is not established, against the view (Sandberg) that mechanism-first recognition is common in this prize.
B040 (orexin) and B008 are named in the statements only as lower-ranked or alternative options, and their maturity is not contested in the round-1 files beyond the credit problems above.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann (count not audited) on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy, and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard; neither involves a credited name on B043, B010 or B005. He also notes that his opening ballot ranked B014 eighth and that clinical familiarity with Parkinson's disease should not inflate it.
Perlmann discloses co-authorship with Ronald Evans, Johan Ericson, Svenningsson and El-Manira; none concerns a shortlisted credited name. He records his role as Secretary as a process role only.
El-Manira discloses a 2009 paper with Perlmann and a 2019 synthesis with Sten Grillner, and notes that optogenetics is widely used in his field, treated as a disclosure and not as a conflict.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and a shared institution with other members; no credited name is documented as a collaborator, mentor, trainee or colleague.
Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius report no specific conflict for the shortlisted ballots.
questions_for_round2: For B043, which of Mojsov or Knudsen takes the third seat, and what in the primary publication record (who first showed the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide, and the Habener group's role) supports the choice?
Should the B043 citation cover physiology only or physiology plus drug development, and if the latter, can one citation read as a single achievement and not two awards stitched together?

If the committee cannot resolve Mojsov's priority, is the stated fallback (Drucker, Holst and Knudsen) acceptable to the three members who now prefer the Mojsov trio, and is the reverse acceptable to the three who prefer the Knudsen trio?
Does any member want a second prize part alongside B043, and if so, can any of B010, B005, B008 or B049 be configured so that the total stays within three laureates?
For B005, should the unit be the discovery and engineering of channelrhodopsin or its application to neurons, and can a defensible trio be named from six credited names?
For B010, how much weight does a basic-mechanism discovery with prospective clinical payoff carry against disease-linked candidates, and does the omission of Ron and Kaufman matter?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete agreement on B043 as the single prize part and on Drucker and Holst, and an even three-three split on the third seat between Mojsov and Knudsen. Members on both sides describe their preference as conditional and say it turns on the framing of the citation and on the primary record of priority. The alternatives are scattered (B010 five times, B005 four, B008 twice, B049 once) and no member prefers a second prize part, so round 2 turns mainly on the third seat.
